# Review pack: Ibrahim's father, Azar

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/azar.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later genealogies give Ibrahim's father a different personal name, and some works treat Azar as a title or as the name of another relative.
- Hadith to add later: reports about Ibrahim and his father on the last day, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Ibrahim speaks to his father  (`#ibrahim-speaks-to-his-father`)

Cited ayat: 6:74, 19:41-48

> **6:74** وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ ءَازَرَ أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَامًا ءَالِهَةً إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰكَ وَقَوْمَكَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ

> **19:41** وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَّبِيًّا
>
> **19:42** إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ لِمَ تَعْبُدُ مَا لَا يَسْمَعُ وَلَا يُبْصِرُ وَلَا يُغْنِى عَنكَ شَيْـًٔا
>
> **19:43** يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى قَدْ جَآءَنِى مِنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ مَا لَمْ يَأْتِكَ فَٱتَّبِعْنِىٓ أَهْدِكَ صِرَٰطًا سَوِيًّا
>
> **19:44** يَٰٓأَبَتِ لَا تَعْبُدِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَصِيًّا
>
> **19:45** يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابٌ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ فَتَكُونَ لِلشَّيْطَٰنِ وَلِيًّا
>
> **19:46** قَالَ أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنْ ءَالِهَتِى يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ وَٱهْجُرْنِى مَلِيًّا
>
> **19:47** قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيْكَ سَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّىٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِى حَفِيًّا
>
> **19:48** وَأَعْتَزِلُكُمْ وَمَا تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَدْعُوا۟ رَبِّى عَسَىٰٓ أَلَّآ أَكُونَ بِدُعَآءِ رَبِّى شَقِيًّا

### Claims

**c1** (6:74): Ibrahim asked his father, Azar, whether he took idols as gods, and said that he saw him and his people in clear error.

**c2** (19:41): The Quran tells the listener to mention Ibrahim in the Book, as one who was truthful, a prophet.

**c3** (19:42): He asked his father why he worshipped what neither hears nor sees nor helps him in any way.

**c4** (19:43): He told his father that knowledge had come to him that had not come to the father, and asked him to follow him so that he would guide him to a level path.

**c5** (19:44-45): He told his father not to worship Satan, who was disobedient to the Merciful, and said that he feared that a punishment from the Merciful would touch him, so that he would become a friend of Satan.

**c6** (19:46): His father asked whether he was turning away from his gods, said that if he did not stop he would stone him, and told him to keep away from him for a long time.

**c7** (19:47-48): Ibrahim answered with a word of peace, said that he would ask his Lord to forgive his father, since his Lord was gracious to him, and said that he would withdraw from them and from what they call on besides God and would call on his Lord, hoping not to be unfortunate in calling on his Lord.

### One-minute summary

Ibrahim asked his father, Azar, why he took idols as gods [c1]. He asked him to follow the knowledge that had come to him and warned him about Satan [c4][c5]. His father threatened to stone him and told him to keep away, and Ibrahim answered with peace and said he would ask his Lord to forgive his father [c6][c7].

### Complete story

Ibrahim asked his father, Azar, whether he took idols as gods, and said that he saw him and his people in clear error [c1]. The Quran tells the listener to mention Ibrahim in the Book, as one who was truthful, a prophet [c2]. He asked his father why he worshipped what neither hears nor sees nor helps him in any way [c3]. He told his father that knowledge had come to him that had not come to the father, and asked him to follow him so that he would guide him to a level path [c4]. He told his father not to worship Satan, who was disobedient to the Merciful, and said that he feared that a punishment from the Merciful would touch him, so that he would become a friend of Satan [c5]. His father asked whether he was turning away from his gods, said that if he did not stop he would stone him, and told him to keep away from him for a long time [c6]. Ibrahim answered with a word of peace, said that he would ask his Lord to forgive his father, since his Lord was gracious to him, and said that he would withdraw from them and from what they call on besides God and would call on his Lord, hoping not to be unfortunate in calling on his Lord [c7].

### Deep study

One passage gives the father's name as Azar [c1]. The other passages say only his father [c3][c6].

### Kids mode

Ibrahim asked his father why he worshipped what cannot hear or see [c3]. His father told him to keep away [c6]. Ibrahim answered with peace and said he would ask his Lord to forgive his father [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Ibrahim answered a threat with a word of peace and a prayer for his father [c6][c7]. Another is that he offered what he had learned and invited his father to follow it [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: whether Azar is the father's personal name, a title, or the name of another relative; the ayah gives the name beside the word father, and readers have differed.
- Not established: where this happened, or when.
- Not established: what the father said or did after the threat.

## 2. Ibrahim turns away  (`#ibrahim-turns-away`)

Cited ayat: 9:114

> **9:114** وَمَا كَانَ ٱسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَن مَّوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُۥٓ أَنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ لِّلَّهِ تَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُ إِنَّ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ لَأَوَّٰهٌ حَلِيمٌ

### Claims

**c1** (9:114): Ibrahim's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him.

**c2** (9:114): When it became clear to Ibrahim that his father was an enemy of God, he disowned him.

**c3** (9:114): Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing.

### One-minute summary

Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father only because of a promise [c1]. When it became clear that his father was an enemy of God, he disowned him [c2].

### Complete story

Ibrahim's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him [c1]. When it became clear to Ibrahim that his father was an enemy of God, he disowned him [c2]. Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing [c3].

### Deep study

The ayah names Ibrahim's father only as his father and does not give a name [c1]. It describes Ibrahim with the Arabic words awwah and halim, usually rendered tender-hearted and forbearing [c3].

### Kids mode

Ibrahim had promised to ask forgiveness for his father [c1]. When he saw that his father was an enemy of God, he turned away from him [c2]. The Quran says that Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah separates a promise that was made from what follows when the truth becomes clear [c1][c2]. Another is that it describes Ibrahim as tender-hearted and forbearing even while he disowns his father [c2][c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: when it became clear to Ibrahim, or how.
- Not established: whether the father was still living at that time.
- Not established: whether the promise in this ayah is the one recorded in the passage where Ibrahim says he will ask forgiveness; connecting them is an inference.
